subject: Pen test report: sharing conditions, redactions, and delivery timeline
messages:
From: security@acme-corp.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: penetration test report & exec summary (NDA/redaction)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for running the engagement with CyberAssure last quarter. Acme's InfoSec team is preparing our external audit packet and would like to review the full penetration test report and a one-page executive summary. Before we proceed, our procurement and legal teams asked for the sharing conditions:

- What NDA do you require for the full report versus the exec summary?
- Can Redwood provide a redacted executive summary now for our audit folder?
- What redaction rubric do you apply (POI, exploit details, internal IP, third-party connectors)?
- Timeline for sharing once legal signs off / PO is issued.

Please loop in anyone on your side who should own the redaction and delivery. If there are specific steps we need to take (e.g., DPAs, data retention terms), let us know.

Best,
Sam Keller
Senior Security Manager
Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: security@acme-corp.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report & exec summary (NDA/redaction)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vivek (Head of Infrastructure Security) and Laura (Legal) to confirm the internal approval and redaction plan. Quick answers up front:

- We can share a redacted executive summary under our standard mutual NDA (we typically use a short mutual confidentiality addendum for pen test reports).
- The full, unredacted pen test report is only released after a signed NDA + evidence/PO process and on a need-to-know basis; often customers request a documented PO or procurement approval before full disclosure.
- Our redaction rubric removes raw exploit chains, internal hostnames and IPs, customer PII, and any third-party secrets; we keep high-level findings, severity, and remediation recommendations. We'll provide a Redaction_Spec worksheet that lists categories.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to propose NDA/wording we need for the full report.
2) Vivek to confirm technical redaction boundaries and whether we can include sanitized PoC excerpts.
3) I can send the redacted exec summary within 48 hours after we align.

Are you able to share a copy of Acme's standard mutual NDA or do you prefer to sign ours? Also, if procurement needs a formal invoice/PO before we send the full report, please share the procurement contact (I see they're cc'd).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Security Liaison | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redaction_Spec_20261202.xlsx (stub)
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, security@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report & exec summary (NDA/redaction)

Marissa / Sam — quick technical note on scope of redactions:

- We will redact: internal IPs/hostnames, live PoCs that include exploit scripts, credentials or API keys, and any customer-specific integration endpoints.
- We will NOT redact: CWE mappings, CVSS scores, remediation steps (high-level), or timelines for remediation performed by Redwood.
- For medium/high risk PoCs, we can provide a paraphrased narrative (no code, no exact commands) that explains impact and mitigations.

If Acme requires more granular info for compliance, we can arrange a scoped read-only session with an assigned Redwood engineer under the NDA and with a conference-room style controlled disclosure. That typically requires a brief SOW amendment and scheduling.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 08:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vivek (Head of Infrastructure Security) and Laura (Legal) to confirm the internal approval and redaction plan.
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, security@acme-corp.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report & exec summary (NDA/redaction)

Hi all — thanks. I reviewed Acme's standard mutual NDA (received via procurement) and recommend the following minimal adjustments before we deliver the unredacted report:

- Add a time-limited access clause: report access expires 90 days after delivery unless a written extension is agreed.
- Prohibit re-sharing outside the named signatories and require secure deletion after the retention period.
- Include an acknowledgment that the report contains Redwood-owned tooling signatures and redaction exceptions (we will mark any content that cannot be redacted without losing the utility of the finding).

For the exec summary, we are fine with the mutual NDA as-is; no additional terms required. For the full report, procurement's PO (or a signed SOW amendment) should be present; we will not release the detailed exploit artifacts until the PO is received and the NDA is countersigned.

Neha — please prepare a redacted executive summary and the Redaction_Spec worksheet. Marissa, I suggest we send the exec summary and the spec to Acme under the mutual NDA and include a link to a DocuSign for the full-report NDA/terms.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Final: exec summary (redacted) delivered; next steps for full report

Hi Sam — sending the redacted executive summary and the redaction spec per Laura's guidance.

What I'm attaching now:
- Redwood_Exec_Summary_Redacted_v1.pdf (redacted: hostnames/IPs removed; PoC narratives paraphrased; severity buckets retained)
- Redaction_Spec_20261202.xlsx (rubric for categories and examples)

Next steps for the full, unredacted report:
1) Please countersign the mutual NDA (DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/ABCDEF123456) — Laura has proposed a 90-day access window for unredacted material.
2) Once we receive the signed NDA + procurement PO (Acme PO #12345), we'll schedule the secure transfer. The PO can be sent to procurement@redwood.com and cc'd to me.
3) If Acme prefers a controlled read-only session instead of file transfer, we can provide that after paperwork is complete; it typically takes 1-2 business days to schedule.

If you want an earlier read-only briefing (no artifacts), I can arrange a 30-minute call with Vivek and the engineer who validated remediation.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into your audit packet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Security Liaison | Redwood Inference
